correctness.rationale: PASS: Zero coefficients split off a cube factor. With at most three nonzero coefficients, the intrinsic section is a centrally symmetric polygon or segment and is a zonotope. When A≥sum remaining coefficients, solving for largest coordinate makes K(a) the affine graph of an (n−1)-cube, including equality. If m≥4 and A<sum others, x1=−1 produces a full-dimensional off-center cube section with r=m−1≥3 and t=A>0. The off-center lemma proves a centrally symmetric section would require some coefficient dominating its absolute offset plus all remaining weights; impossible as each remaining a_k≤A and other positive terms remain. The lemma’s facet proof is sound: in dimension r−1, pairwise nonparallel coordinate facet normals imply each facet-coordinate center c_i=0, boundedness needs at least r−1 facet coordinates, t≠0 excludes all r, so the sole non-facet inequality is redundant, forcing the dominance inequality. Thus this proper exposed face is not centrally symmetric, ruling out zonoids (exposed faces of zonoids are zonoids). Independently enumerated 289 exact rational nondominant 4-coordinate faces and 896 off-center 3-cube lemmas, plus dominant cases; these tests corroborate but are not proof.
residual_risks: This is for hyperplane CENTRAL cube slices only; does not classify arbitrary zonotope sections.

originality.rationale: PASS (best-of-knowledge): Anantharaman gives non-zonoid cube-section examples, sufficient dominant coefficient hypotheses and explicitly acknowledges the missing general necessity case, not this iff for every n and support size. The Resultary Haar-random 4-cube face-vector law has the generic normal dominance cut but does not characterize deterministic zonoids in every dimension, including equality and zero coordinates. Classical zonotope face symmetry criterion plus the proved specific off-center lemma does not mechanically supply this classification without the lemma.
